main_body: Flat dark-green ground patch (4x3 tiles) with scattered grass tufts and tiny coloured flower dots; terrain tile, not a standing object
top_band: none - flat ground texture, no top/front structure expected for terrain
evidence: Terrain ground patch: a repeating 16px tile of dark olive green with grass-blade tufts, brown pebbles and yellow/red flower dots. No standing volume, so the 3/4 top/front contract does not apply; no side faces or elevation drawing present. The column scan shows only repeating tile texture rows, consistent with a ground autotile.

style.evidence: Candidate has 12 distinct colours and a median of 12 per tile, above the paving reference (7) but well below the grass reference (26 per tile, 80 colours). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the texture is made of sparse blade tufts in 3-4 greens over a base green plus rare flower dots. The pattern repeats identically every 16px in a visibly tiled grid (same tufts and flowers at identical positions in each tile), which looks mechanical next to the grass reference's varied clumps. Ramps are shallow: base green, a lighter blade, a darker shadow and a few accent pixels. No outlines, so the outline criterion is not applicable. Compared with the grass reference it is thinner and less varied in material craft, and the identical repeating tufts and obvious tile seams make it read as a stamped pattern.
